objective: Identify the expansion and high-terminal-bank mechanisms used by current leading agents, then add a bounded land-payback branch that can raise v0.7.1-i5's ceiling without weakening its control results.

success_gates.evidence: At least two current high-bank public replays with day-level land, labor, engine, and bank transitions.
success_gates.candidate_comparison: Both seats against v0.7.1-i5 plus a bounded persona sanity suite.
success_gates.upper_cap: Candidate must show a materially higher terminal bank on at least one expansion-favorable seed.
success_gates.runtime: Target under 250 ms; reject any action above 700 ms.

boundaries: Stop after two resumed policy iterations
findings: Two current-leader replays were action-identical for the first 144 turns, then diverged as environment and opponent signals accumulated.

The high-bank path is a coupled cascade: 12 melon, 7 wheat, 2 cows, 2 sheep, five opening hires, second quadrant near day 6, third near day 11, recurring crops, mixed livestock, fertilizer sales, and 8-12 daily hands.
Protected expansion labor plus a twelve-hand service cap reduced the fixed-seed deficit versus v0.7.1-i5 from roughly 13k to an average 1,755.
The final arena still finished 1-7 and never reached 60k bank by day 24, so v0.7.2 does not replace v0.7.1-i5.
next_hypothesis: Make expansion conditional on estimated service-adjusted return versus a lean-engine counterfactual, rather than assuming the frontier cascade is always the highest-value branch.
